techniques.name: Sobol Indices
techniques.description: Sobol indices show how much of the variation in a model's output can be traced to each of its inputs. The analyst sets a range or probability distribution for every input and runs the model on a large, carefully designed sample of input combinations. The variance (spread) of the outputs is then split into shares. A first-order index is the share caused by one input varying on its own, and a total-order index also counts every interaction that input takes part in. A large gap between the two signals that an input matters mainly through interactions, and optional second-order indices show which pairs of inputs interact.

example_use_cases.description: Analysing a climate prediction model to determine which atmospheric parameters (temperature, humidity, pressure) contribute most to rainfall forecast uncertainty, helping meteorologists understand which measurements need the highest precision.

A risk team validating a portfolio valuation model asks which economic indicators (interest rates, inflation, GDP growth) drive most of the variation in predicted portfolio value. A large gap between an indicator's total-order and first-order indices shows it acts mainly through interactions, which tells the team which scenarios to stress-test together.

limitations.description: The standard sampling scheme needs N(2D+2) model runs for D inputs (N(D+2) without second-order indices), with N often in the thousands. A slow model, or one with dozens of inputs, quickly becomes impractical. Grouping related inputs, or screening first with a cheaper method such as Morris, reduces the cost.

Assumes the inputs vary independently. If real inputs are correlated, for example income and postcode, the sample contains combinations the model never meets in practice, and the indices can mislead about which inputs matter.

Needs a probability distribution or range for every input, and the indices depend on that choice, because widening one input's range raises its share of the variance. If the ranges do not reflect the real deployment population, the ranking describes a model the users will never face.

Variance is the only yardstick. When the output is heavily skewed or has several peaks, variance shares can be unreliable guides to which inputs matter, and a moment-independent method such as PAWN may suit better.

Estimates carry sampling error. With too few runs the confidence intervals can be as wide as the indices themselves, so small indices cannot be told apart from zero. Report the intervals SALib returns and check that the ranking holds when N is increased.

resources.title: Global sensitivity indices for nonlinear mathematical models and their Monte Carlo estimates
Importance measures in global sensitivity analysis of nonlinear models
A novel feature selection method based on global sensitivity analysis with application in machine learning-based prediction model
resources.abstract: Feature selection (FS) is vitally important for determining the optimum subsets of features with effective information and maximizing the model accuracy. This study proposes a novel FS method based on global sensitivity analysis (GSA) for effectively determining the most relevant feature subsets and improving prediction performance of machine learning (ML)based models. Feature ranking is determined based on the results obtained from three global sensitivity analysis (GSA) including Pearson, Sobol’ and PAWN. This novel GSA-based FS method is applied to engineering practice with the combination of ML algorithm random forest (RF) to predict tunnelling-induced settlement prediction model. Meanwhile, the feature extraction method principle component analysis (PCA) is also used to develop RF-based model for comparing the performance of proposed GSA-based FS method. The results indicate the novel GSA-based FS method effectively determines the significance of input variables. The prediction performance of RF-based model with the integration of GSA-based FS methods is enhanced dramatically, and obviously outperforms the model with the integration of PCA-based dimensionality reduction method.

sample_claims.text: Our flood-model review reports atmospheric inputs' main and total shares of output variance under the documented independent input distributions.
The portfolio-model audit records first and total-order sensitivity indices, distinguishing main effects from overall interaction involvement.
Our clinical-model sensitivity review reports patient-input variance shares under the chosen distributions, without treating them as a decomposition of every source of prediction uncertainty.

techniques.name: Causal Mediation Analysis in Language Models
techniques.description: Causal mediation analysis traces which internal components of a language model carry the effect of a change in the input to the output. The analyst makes a controlled change to the input, such as swapping 'nurse' for 'man' in a prompt, and measures how the model's next-word probabilities shift. To find the indirect effect through one component (a single neuron, or an attention head, which is the part of the model that chooses which earlier words to focus on), they feed the model the original input but give that component the value it took on the changed input. To find the direct effect, they feed the changed input but hold that component at its original value. Repeating this across many components shows where in the network a behaviour is carried.

example_use_cases.description: A safety team finds that a language model gives unsafe medical advice when a request is phrased as an instruction rather than a question. They compare outputs for the two phrasings and use mediation analysis to find which attention heads carry most of the shift in the probability of the unsafe reply, so a fix can target those heads and the analysis can be rerun to check it worked.

A research team studying why a language model sometimes gets subject-verb agreement wrong in sentences with an intervening clause changes the number of the subject noun and measures the shift in the verb's probability. Mediation analysis then shows which neurons carry the number information, and whether the same neurons are used across sentence structures.

limitations.description: Needs white-box access and knowledge of the architecture. The analyst must read and overwrite activations at chosen points inside the model, so it cannot be used on a model offered only through an API, and a poorly chosen intervention point can give misleading conclusions.

Conclusions hold for the contrast tested. Swapping 'nurse' for 'man' and tracking one probability ratio tests a single contrast, and a different prompt set or outcome measure can point to different components. Effects also differ between models: larger GPT-2 models showed larger effects, and masked language models matched less well.

Every component and every prompt needs its own forward passes, so testing all the neurons or heads of a large model on many prompts is expensive. Analysts often test a subset or groups of components, which can miss effects elsewhere in the network.

Single-component effects do not simply add up. Vig et al. found that intervening on all neurons together produced an effect far larger than the sum of the single-neuron effects, so ranking components one at a time can understate or misplace where a behaviour is carried.

The split into direct and indirect effects is not guaranteed to be exact. In a non-linear network the total effect need not equal their sum, and Vig et al. report only an approximate match for GPT-2, so the split should be checked rather than assumed.

resources.title: Investigating Gender Bias in Language Models Using Causal Mediation Analysis
resources.abstract: Common methods for interpreting neural models in natural language processing typically examine either their structure or their behavior, but not both. We propose a methodology grounded in the theory of causal mediation analysis for interpreting which parts of a model are causally implicated in its behavior. It enables us to analyze the mechanisms by which information flows from input to output through various model components, known as mediators. We apply this methodology to analyze gender bias in pre-trained Transformer language models. We study the role of individual neurons and attention heads in mediating gender bias across three datasets designed to gauge a model's sensitivity to gender bias. Our mediation analysis reveals that gender bias effects are (i) sparse, concentrated in a small part of the network; (ii) synergistic, amplified or repressed by different components; and (iii) decomposable into effects flowing directly from the input and indirectly through the mediators.

resources.title: Causal Analysis of Syntactic Agreement Mechanisms in Neural Language Models
resources.abstract: Targeted syntactic evaluations have demonstrated the ability of language models to perform subject-verb agreement given difficult contexts. To elucidate the mechanisms by which the models accomplish this behavior, this study applies causal mediation analysis to pre-trained neural language models. We investigate the magnitude of models’ preferences for grammatical inflections, as well as whether neurons process subject-verb agreement similarly across sentences with different syntactic structures. We uncover similarities and differences across architectures and model sizes—notably, that larger models do not necessarily learn stronger preferences. We also observe two distinct mechanisms for producing subject-verb agreement depending on the syntactic structure of the input sentence. Finally, we find that language models rely on similar sets of neurons when given sentences with similar syntactic structure.

sample_claims.text: On the tested prompts, most of the effect of the input change on the language model's output is carried by a small number of attention heads, each with a measured indirect effect.
The model's subject-verb agreement behaviour is carried by identifiable neurons that are reused across sentences of similar structure.
The shift in the probability of the unsafe reply caused by the instruction phrasing is mediated mainly by identified components, and the finding is reproduced on held-out prompts.
After mitigation is applied to the components identified as carrying the unsafe behaviour, rerunning the same analysis shows a reduced indirect effect.
